**Step 1 — Scene:** A chicken and penne salad with leafy greens, small vegetables, and a creamy dressing.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a 26 cm circular approximation gives an area of **3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Sliced cooked chicken breast, penne pasta, mixed leafy greens, cherry tomatoes, other salad vegetables (visible carrot and cucumber-like pieces), and creamy dressing. No separate quantity of oil can be reliably identified.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:** Area shares are allocated between ingredients to avoid counting overlapping layers twice.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chicken breast | 28% | 149 cm² × 1.5 cm = 223 ml | 0.95 | 211 g | 165 | 348 kcal |
| Cooked penne | 14% | 74 cm² × 1.2 cm = 89 ml | 0.8 | 71 g | 155 | 110 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 32% | 170 cm² × 2.5 cm = 425 ml | 0.15 | 64 g | 20 | 13 kcal |
| Cherry tomatoes | 3% | 16 cm² × 2 cm = 32 ml | 0.6 | 19 g | 18 | 3 kcal |
| Other salad vegetables | 4% | 21 cm² × 1 cm = 21 ml | 0.6 | 13 g | 30 | 4 kcal |
| Creamy dressing | 3% | 16 cm² × 1.5 cm = 24 ml* | 1.0 | 24 g | 300 | 72 kcal |

*The dressing volume represents the collected equivalent of the coating and small pools, not a uniform layer.*

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** The allocated areas total **84%** of the plate, consistent with the visible coverage. Approximately **402 g and 550 kcal** is plausible for this substantial chicken salad with a modest amount of pasta. Dressing composition and chicken thickness are the largest uncertainties.
